primitives.breakdown_regime: When P_{\text{catch}} = 0, then P_{\text{run}}(y) = 0 for all y.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is the expected fantasy point calculation per target, derived from two probabilistic models: completion probability (CP) and yards-after-catch (xYAC). Each pass play contributes to expected points through a product of catch probability and yardage probability, weighted by PPR scoring rules. The model assumes that the average receiver's performance can be estimated via these probabilistic components. The key insight is that high-volume players near the goal line contribute disproportionately due to higher TD probability. The failure mode occurs when the model underestimates variance in skill or misrepresents the distribution of YAC outcomes. The dual nature of the problem lies in separating the probability of making a play from the value of that play. The kernel of the computation is the convolution of CP and YAC distributions to yield expected PPR points per target. This framework enables dynamic evaluation of player performance against expectations, identifying overperformers and underperformers.
